The core mathematical structure emerges from a sensor-driven telemetry system that interfaces with remote coaching environments. The sensor fusion operator (D(t)) aggregates multi-modal inputs into a coherent data stream for downstream processing. The performance monitoring kernel (P(S,t)) applies sport-specific transformations to extract meaningful performance indicators. The remote coaching interface (R(I,M)) enables real-time feedback loops between athlete and coach. These operators form a hierarchical Bayesian network where D(t) feeds P(S,t), which in turn informs R(I,M). Dualities arise in the temporal symmetry of data acquisition and feedback control. Failure modes include signal degradation, kernel misalignment, and communication latency exceeding acceptable thresholds. The system exhibits robustness under controlled environmental conditions but degrades predictably when assumptions about data integrity or coach responsiveness are violated.
